newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court interprets Community rules on sugar levies.
newsitem.headline: Court interprets Community rules on sugar levies.

text.p: The European Court of Justice said on Thursday Community rules on sugar create an obligation to pay storage levies when sugar is disposed of, not at the time of production.

Production levy obligations arise, however, when the sugar production is calculated at the end of each year. The levy is to be calculated "by dividing the estimated overall loss by the estimated production ... attributable to the current market year," the court said.
For elimination levy calculation, the court told taxing authorities to look at production of sugar in the 1986/87 marketing years.

French tax authorities demanded additional tax from sugar manufacturer, Sucrerie de Maizy (now Sucrerie de Berneuil-sur-Aisne) for tax years 1985/1986 to cover production, storage, elimination and special elimination levies.

The court would not interpret the French term, "le fait generateur" (the chargeable event) because the same language is not used in Community rules on sugar levies. "It is not for the court to give a ruling on the meaning of a term in national law," the court said. The Community language used rather than chargeable event is "prescribed conditions for materialization of the obligation to pay the ... levies."
EXCERPTS FROM THE JUDGMENT
(Court translation into English. Original language of the case: French)
"Common organization of the markets in the sugar sector - Chargeable event for storage, production and elimination levies - Period in respect of which elimination levies are payable"
In Case C-172/95
24 October 1996
Reference from the Tribunal Administratif, Amiens (France) for a preliminary ruling in the proceedings pending before that court between
Societe Sucriere Agricole de Maizy
Soicete Sucriere de Berneuil-sur-Aisne
and
Directeur Regional des Impots
on the interpretation of the Community rules relating to various levies in the sugar sector
THE COURT hereby rules

1. Article 8(2), third subparagraph (a), of Council Regulation (EEC) No 1785/81 of 30 June 1981 on the common organization of the markets in the sugar sector and article 6(4) of Council Regulation (EEC) No 1358/77 of 20 June 1977 iaying down general rules for offsetting storage costs for sugar and repealing regulation (EEC) No 750/68 must be interpreted as meaning that the prescribed conditions for materialization of the obligation to pay the storage levy are satisfied when the sugar is disposed of.

2. Article 28(3) and (4) of Regulation No 1785/81 must be interpreted as meaning that the prescribed conditions for materialization of the obligation to pay the production levies thereby imposed are satisfied whe sugar production is calculated at the end of each marketing year.

3. Article 32a(1) of regulation 1785/8l, as amended by Council regulation (EEC) No 934/86 of 24 March 1986, and Article 1(1) of Commission Regulation (EEC) No 3046/86 of 3 October 1996 laying down detailed rules concerning the collection of the elimination levy in the sugar sector must be interpreted as meaning that the prescribed conditions for materialization of the obligation to pay the elimination levy are satisfied when sugar production is calculated at the end or each of the marketing years from 1986/87 to 1990/91.

4. Article 1 of Council Regulation (EEC) No 1914/87 of 2 July 1987 introducing a special elimination levy in the sugar sector for the 1986/87 marketing year and Articles 1 and 2 of Commission Regulation (EEC) No 3061/87 of 13 October 1997 fixing the coefficient for the calculation of the special elimination levy in the sugar sector for the 1986/87 marketing year must be interpreted as meaning that the prescribed conditions for materialization of the obligation to pay the special elimination levy are satisfied when sugar production is calculated at the end of the 1986/87 marketing year.
